title: Peruvian Roast Chicken
subtitle: Whole roast chicken with cumin, paprika, and lime
excerpt: A whole chicken marinated in cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, and garlic then roasted until the skin is deeply coloured and the meat is juicy. Served with lime wedges, this delivers bold flavour with very little effort.
sourceNotes: Pollo a la brasa, Peru's famous roast chicken, was developed in Lima in the 1950s by Swiss immigrant Roger Schuler, who combined a local charcoal rotisserie technique with Andean spices. The dish spread rapidly across Peru and later around the world as a definitive example of Peruvian street food culture.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the chicken up to 24 hours ahead in the fridge for deeper flavour.

content.text: Push the marinade under the skin as well as rubbing it on the surface. This flavours the meat directly rather than just the exterior.

items.prepNote: 1 juiced, 1 cut into wedges to serve

content.text: Mix the garlic, spices, oregano, olive oil, and lime juice into a thick paste. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Pat the chicken dry. Use your fingers to loosen the skin over the breast and thighs. Push half the marinade under the skin and rub the rest all over the outside of the bird.

Place the chicken breast-side up in the roasting tin. Roast at 200 C for 1 hour 20 minutes, or until the juices run clear when you pierce the thigh at its thickest point. A probe thermometer should read 75 C at the thickest part of the thigh.
Rest the chicken loosely covered with foil for 10 minutes before carving. Serve with lime wedges.

items.symptom: Skin is pale and not coloured
items.cause: Marinade was too wet or oven not hot enough
items.fix: Pat the chicken dry before marinating and use a fully preheated oven.
Use a probe thermometer and rest covered with foil.

items.symptom: Garlic tastes raw in the finished dish
items.cause: Paste was spread too thickly under the skin
items.fix: Mix garlic thoroughly with oil and acid before applying.
